what_happened: With a RIGHT command and the recorded path to its right, the ego drifted left into the bus's lane (actor 127). It then closed on the slow or stopped bus at about 8 m/s, with the gap falling from 36 m to 7.6 m, and braked only slightly before hitting the bus's rear with its front.

The command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted left of the recorded path, ending about 7 m off it, into the lane of a slow bus (actor 127). It closed on the bus from about 36 m to impact while only slowing from 8.7 to 7.4 m/s, and rear-ended it with its front.

The command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted left away from the recorded path into the lane of bus 127, which had turned into the road ahead and was moving slowly. The ego kept going at about 8 m/s while the gap shrank from 22 m to 7 m, barely braked, and hit the back of the bus.

With a RIGHT command, the ego stayed in a left lane about 8 m away from where the human drove, then ran into the rear of bus 127, which had angled into the lane ahead and was slower. The bus was visible for more than 2 s, but the ego only eased from 7.5 to 5.6 m/s and hit it head-on.

Approaching an intersection with a RIGHT command, the ego left the recorded path, which went to the right, and drifted left behind lead car 9. Its planned path kept bending left, and while slowing from 10.8 to 5.4 m/s it ran onto the edge of the median island on the left (offroad; 7.6 m off the recorded path at 10.2 s). The input JSON also flags a front collision, but the frames' metrics table shows collision_front at 0, so the offroad is the clear failure.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, but the policy kept heading straight and drifted left while slowing from 12 to 7 m/s. By 9.5 s it was 7.5 m off the recorded track and had run onto the median/edge on the left side of the road before the intersection. No actor was close (the nearest one ahead was over 20 m away), so the ego simply steered off the drivable area.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego stayed in the straight lane about 5.7 m off the human's path and closed on actor 9, which was slowing for a red light. The ego slowed from 12.4 to 5.1 m/s, but not soon or hard enough: the gap shrank from 15.2 m to 4.5 m and the ego hit the car's rear with its front.

With a RIGHT command at a large signalized intersection, the policy planned a path that kept bending left while the recorded route curved right. The ego slowed from 11.5 to 5.9 m/s, ended up about 7.5 m left of the human trajectory, and drove onto the median nose at the stop line. No other actor was involved, and the camera view stayed reasonable until the end.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path bore right toward the turn lanes. Instead, the ego slowed from 12 to 7 m/s while drifting left, away from that path. By 9.4 s it had run onto the gravel median nose left of the travel lanes, about 7.5 m off the recorded trajectory. The camera view looked clean before the failure, so a rendering problem doesn't explain the policy's steering.
